newsitem.title: UK: Britain to shake up overseas telecoms market - FT.
newsitem.headline: Britain to shake up overseas telecoms market - FT.

text.p: Britain is set to make its largest single move towards opening up its international telecoms market to competition, the Financial Times newspaper said on Wednesday.

Licenses will be given to all 46 companies seeking to compete with British Telecommunications Plc and Mercury Communications in offering a full range of telecoms services between Britain and the rest of the world, the paper said. The licenses will be effective from January 1.
Until now companies other than BT and Mercury have only been able to operate by leasing lines from one of the two British companies.
The move could entice substantial inward investment but might also result in a significant fall in overseas telecoms revenues, the paper said.
The decision might also defuse opposition by AT&T, the largest U.S. long-distance carrier, to the proposed $20-billion merger of BT and MCI Communications, it said.
AT&T argued the deal should be blocked by the U.S. authorities because the British market was not yet fully open.
The list of applicants for the international licenses include AT&T, Eurotunnel and Globel One -- the alliance between Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom.
"All are expected to be approved and the Department of Trade and Industry wants to issue the licences in a single block before the Christmas break," the FT said.
